turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, come through. What seems to be the trouble today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (CAREGIVER): It's his eyes, doctor. We only got back from Morocco on Sunday and—
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Yellow.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yellow, yes. Let me have a look. Mm, the whites have gone quite yellow. When did you first clock that?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Thursday.
[SEG0006] person_2 (CAREGIVER): So that's five days, roughly. And his wee has gone really dark, like stewed tea.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dark as well. And in yourself, how are you feeling?
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Knackered.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tired. Yellow eyes, dark urine, tiredness after a trip, so I'm already thinking about the liver, but let me not get ahead of myself. What were you eating out there?
[SEG0010] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Roadside stalls, mostly. Little grill places, chicken, salad, the odd—
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Chicken.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chicken off the stalls. Did anyone else on the trip get ill?
[SEG0013] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Two of the lads had the runs for a couple of days. He's the only one who's gone yellow, mind.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay. So the others had diarrhoea, and he's the one with the jaundice. Do you drink alcohol at all?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0016] person_2 (CAREGIVER): He doesn't touch it. Never has, not even on—
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not even on holiday. Good, that takes a heavy night off the table. Any fever? Felt hot, or shivery?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): No fever. And a cough, or any bother with your breathing?
[SEG0020] person_2 (CAREGIVER): He was a bit chesty last winter, but that's long—
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, I do need it from him. Any cough now?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Has the skin been itchy at all?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Sort of.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sort of itchy, or not really?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Not really.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hmm. Bit mixed, that. I'll leave it. Err, any tablets, prescribed or ones you bought?
[SEG0028] person_2 (CAREGIVER): On holiday he had some crocin, for a headache. And at home it's the water tablet, once a day.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Crocin, that's paracetemol, yes. How many did you take?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Two.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two tablets. Do you know the strength?
[SEG0032] person_2 (CAREGIVER): The five hundred ones, I think. He only did that the one day. The water tablet, umm, I can never remember the proper—
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): Bendro.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bendroflumethazide. Is that the two point five milligram one?
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0036] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Yes, two point five, every morning, for his blood pressure. Been on it years.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): So the blood pressure is a known thing, and you're on bendroflumethazide two point five milligrams each morning. And the crocin was a one-off, you're not still taking it.
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. I'd rather you didn't take any more paracetemol while the liver might be under strain. Fluids, rest, and no more of that stall food for now.
[SEG0040] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Should we be worried? His sister had something with her—

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me think it through. Yellow eyes means the bilirubin is up, the dark wee fits, and the timing after street food makes me think of a hepatitis, possibly hepatitis A, seeing as the others had tummy upset. It could still be a stone or a reaction, and I'm not calling it either way until the bloods.
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): What I want today is bloods. Liver tests, the full set, and hepatitis serology, A, B and C. I'll book both of those now, downstairs in phlebotomy.
[SEG0044] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Today?
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Today, yes. They're ordered. I want to see him again next Wednesday with the results, whether he's picked up or not.
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): Okay.
[SEG0047] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Of. We'll be there. He keeps taking the bendro?

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, carry on with the bendro as usual. Uh, if he goes more yellow, starts vomiting, or gets confused, don't wait until Wednesday, come straight in. Otherwise I'll see you next Wednesday.

spec.situation: Person with yellow eyes, dark urine and tiredness after eating at roadside stalls on a trip; others at the trip also ill; alcohol denied; liver blood tests and hepatitis serology planned.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

bad.reason: Crocin/paracetamol for headache, one day, no longer taking; 500 mg is uncertain ('I think').
bad.text: crocin (generic_name=paracetamol, dose=500 mg, duration=1 day, indication=headache, status=discontinued, reported_by=caregiver)

omissions.text: Recent travel history: returned from Morocco on Sunday.
Possible exposure/history: ate roadside stall food including chicken and salad while in Morocco.
Others on the trip had diarrhoea for a couple of days; patient was the only one to develop jaundice.
Negative finding: no shortness of breath/breathing trouble when asked.
Itching was specifically asked about and not clearly present: patient initially said 'sort of' but then clarified 'not really'.
Paracetamol/Crocin dose quantity was two tablets taken on one day (total 1 g if 500 mg tablets).
Hepatitis serology was specified as hepatitis A, B and C.
Blood tests were booked downstairs in phlebotomy today.
Follow-up instruction included returning next Wednesday whether he has improved or not.
